Date: 2028-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: p95 spike on model v9q - urgent: rollback criteria?

Hi Irene / Kimberly,

We observed a sustained p95 latency increase from our fleet calling model v9q (hosted via Redwood) starting 09/16 07:40 UTC. Over the last 2 hours p95 has been ~1.8s above contract baseline and is causing timeouts in our payment flows (we've seen ~0.6% user-facing failures).

Can you confirm whether this meets your rollback trigger or SLA relief criteria? We need a decision within the hour — if not, we will implement client-side throttles which will materially affect our throughput.

I've attached a condensed incident log and a sample traffic snapshot.

Thanks,
Alex M.
SRE, CoreBank

Attachments: incident_log.csv (text/csv), traffic_snapshot.jsonl (application/jsonl)

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: CoreBank SRE <sre@corebank.com>, Alex M. <alex@corebank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-16T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike on model v9q - urgent: rollback criteria?

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. We're pulling telemetry now but a quick summary up-front:

- Preliminary root-cause points to a quantized kernel path interaction specific to v9q-tiny-quant that surfaces at sequence lengths > 512. CoreBank traffic spike included a higher-than-usual proportion of long sequences (attached snapshot).
- Per contract, a sustained p95 delta > 1.5s for >30 minutes that correlates with model variant changes qualifies for provisional rollback consideration; we are seeing ~2 hours but need to validate correlation.

Immediate plan (provisional, pending internal approvals below):
1) Pin CoreBank traffic to the compatible non-quant variant v9q-std for a rolling 15-minute diversion window (this avoids full account rollback and keeps SLA met).
2) If monitoring during diversion shows p95 normalizes within the SLO window, we'll keep traffic pinned and schedule a formal model variant rollback for the account (requires approval from Product & Ops).
3) If pin/diversion is ineffective or introduces degradation elsewhere, we will escalate to a full rollback of v9q-tiny-quant for the region and open a temporary SLO carveout for CoreBank while remediation proceeds.

Kimberly / Markus — can you confirm the feasibility of a targeted pin to v9q-std for CoreBank and whether there are any capacity constraints? Also attaching an early analysis graph (analysis_p95_graph.png).

Alex — please confirm that a targeted diversion is acceptable on your side and whether you prefer traffic split (95/5) for staged validation.

Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: analysis_p95_graph.png (image/png)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike on model v9q - urgent: rollback criteria?

Irene / team — quick technical note:

- Confirmed: the v9q-tiny-quant kernel has a regression when KV cache is rehydrated beyond the 512 token boundary. The hit is in the attention combinator path; p95 increases observed locally replicate CoreBank's traces.
- Capacity: we have spare capacity on v9q-std in us-west pool; pinning CoreBank temporarily (all prod traffic) to v9q-std is feasible and will not breach other customers' allocations if staged over 15 minutes.
- Risk: v9q-std is ~1.2x more costly per token; need Product approval for temporary cost delta and Ops sign-off for the pin window.

If Product signs off, I can trigger a diversion at 2028-09-16T12:00:00-07:00 and leave a 30-minute guarded observation period. We'll stream p95 to the incident board and auto-revert if error rates exceed 0.5%.

-Markus
Director, Serving Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Team / Alex — following the technical validation and cost estimate discussion, Product and Finance have approved a provisional SLO hold for CoreBank tied to deal RBW-34729. Approval details below:

- Authorization: Temporary SLO hold (p95 delta tolerance) granted from 2028-09-16T12:00:00-07:00 through 2028-09-18T18:00:00-07:00 while we stabilize via targeted diversion.
- Traffic plan: 100% pin to v9q-std for the first 30 minutes, then 95/5 staged split for 60 minutes, monitoring p95 and error rates.
- Acceptance criteria to lift hold: sustained p95 within SLA for 2 consecutive 1-hour windows and error rate <0.2%.
- Cost handling: temporary cost delta will be reconciled against RBW-34729 usage credits; Procurement (procurements@corebank.com) has been CC'd to start paperwork if needed.

Markus has scheduled the diversion and will execute the guarded roll at 12:00 PDT. Monica, please ensure the observability dashboard (SUP-9123) is updated with playbook steps and automated alerts.

Alex — please confirm you have updated timeout thresholds on your client side to avoid duplicate requests during the pin.

Kimberly Park
